paragraphs.source_en: My heart and mind had all been occupied with the thoughts of Kiyo, when all at once bang, bang, bang, just above my head, came the sound of drumming feet on the floor made by some thirty or forty boys in number. I feared that the floor might come down upon my head. The drumming was followed by a war cry proportionately loud. Thinking something serious had happened, I sprang out of my bed. Then, only then, it struck me that the boys had done it out of vengeance. No crime could be canceled before a man apologized, confessing what he had done was wrong. His conscience would tell him he had done wrong. A right-minded man would go to bed and repent there from the bottom of his heart and come to ask
